jane_customer: Hey @support — hitting a weird retry bug with the Python SDK (v0.8.2). We POST to /v1/predictions and when the service returns 429 then a 504 for the same request, our app sees the operation processed twice (duplicate side effects). Not using an idempotency header right now.

ian_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the minimal repro + logs? Also which exact SDK package (pip name) and Python version?

jane_customer: Repro is trivial: fast retries at ~200 req/s from a small worker pool. Code snippet:```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
resp = client.predictions.create(model='text-gen-1', input='...')
```
Logs (sanitized):
```
2025-11-03T12:11:23.456Z INFO request POST /v1/predictions id=abc123 -> 429
2025-11-03T12:11:23.458Z WARN retry: attempt=1 sleep=0.0 (jitter) 
2025-11-03T12:11:23.459Z INFO request POST /v1/predictions id=abc123 -> 504
2025-11-03T12:11:23.460Z WARN retry: attempt=2 sleep=0.0 (jitter)
2025-11-03T12:11:23.461Z INFO request POST /v1/predictions id=abc123 -> 200 processed
2025-11-03T12:11:23.462Z INFO request POST /v1/predictions id=abc123 -> 200 processed
```
Both 200s are different downstream jobs.

devx_liz: Thanks, that log line showing sleep=0.0 stands out. Can you confirm pip show redwood-inference (exact package name) and ``pip freeze | grep redwood``?

jane_customer: ``redwood==0.8.2``; Python 3.11.6.``pip freeze`` shows only that package.

eng_ryan: This sounds like the jitter/backoff function returning 0 consistently under high CPU contention. There's an edge where random.random() * base_delay can underflow in our current backoff wrapper when base_delay is a numpy float64 — yields 0.0 after cast.

ian_support: Would you be able to attach a HAR or capture tcpdump+request ids? If not, can you temporarily set an Idempotency-Key header as a workaround? E.g.:```python
resp = client.predictions.create(..., headers={'Idempotency-Key': uuid.uuid4().hex})
```
This should prevent duplicate processing until we patch.

jane_customer: I can try the Idempotency-Key patch, but this is a library bug, not our app. Any ETA on a fix?

sre_alex: We've reproduced locally with a small harness. Root cause: when backoff base delay comes from a decimal-like type we mistakenly cast before applying jitter, and our jitter multiplier was allowed to be 0.0 in some code paths. Repro steps we used: stress loop sending 500 concurrent requests to a test endpoint and injecting 429/504 responses.

devx_liz: Short-term: set env var REDWOOD_RETRY_MAX_JITTER=0.2 or pass retry config to the client to force non-zero jitter. Example: ```python
client = RedwoodClient(..., retry={'backoff_base':0.5, 'jitter':0.2})
```
Works around the float-cast path.

eng_ryan: We're preparing a patch in runtime/backoff.py to ensure jitter is computed after float conversion and to clamp min jitter to 1e-3. We'll cut a 0.8.3-rc today.

ops-bot: New issue created: INF-4721 "python sdk: jitter/backoff zero sleep on 429/504 -> duplicate requests". Labels: bug, high-priority, needs-repro.

ian_support: @jane_customer can you confirm if you want us to schedule a hotfix release to your account's environment, or would you prefer the RC to test internally first?

jane_customer: Hotfix would be great, we're hitting this in prod. Happy to help test.

devx_liz: Okay I'll coordinate a hotfix roll for your org. Also please add an Idempotency-Key header as a stopgap.

jane_customer: Added Idempotency-Key and throttle lowered. No duplicates observed for the last 10 minutes. Thanks.

eng_ryan: Patch deployed to canary and RC published to pip as `redwood==0.8.3rc1`. Change log: ensure jitter calc after float casting, clamp min jitter >0, add unit tests for Decimal/numpy inputs.

jane_customer: Verified 0.8.3rc1 in staging — no duplicates under previous load pattern.

ian_support: Closing the customer-facing loop. ENG will follow up with post-mortem entry and add e2e tests for idempotency headers + backoff.

jane_customer: Thanks all :heart:
